Assessment
Rosa Colón (MRN SYN-4790974, DOB 1987-12-12) is a 36-year-old G2P1 woman currently in the first trimester of pregnancy (11 weeks at prenatal intake on 2024-05-20; ~13 weeks currently by LMP 2024-03-04) referred for a reactive Trypanosoma cruzi antibody screening test identified at blood donation on 2024-05-06. She has high-risk epidemiologic exposure history: born in rural Cochabamba, Bolivia, where she lived in an adobe house with a thatched roof until age 14 before moving to the United States in 2015. She is completely asymptomatic, denying cardiac symptoms (palpitations, syncope, dyspnea) and gastrointestinal symptoms (dysphagia, constipation). Physical exam and baseline prenatal labs (Hb 12.3 g/dL, WBC 7.2, ALT 14 U/L, Cr 0.6 mg/dL) are unremarkable.

Clinical Assessment: Suspected chronic Chagas disease (indeterminate form, pending cardiac evaluation) in pregnancy. Because a single blood donor screening test does not establish diagnosis, confirmatory serologic testing using two distinct antigenic assays is required. Additionally, baseline evaluation for cardiac involvement with a 12-lead ECG is indicated for all patients with suspected/confirmed chronic T. cruzi inf
